items.q: A bar graph shows lunches sold: Monday 9, Tuesday 21, Wednesday 16. How many more lunches were sold on Tuesday than on Monday?
misconceptions: added the bars instead of comparing them
compared the wrong two days
correct
read Monday's bar instead of the difference
items.why: How many more means compare: 21 - 9 = 12 more lunches on Tuesday.

items.q: On a picture graph, each picture stands for 2 books. One row shows 5 pictures. How many books is that?
misconceptions: counted the pictures and forgot the scale
added the scale instead of multiplying
correct
multiplied 5 by itself instead of by the scale
items.why: The scale is the key: each picture is worth 2 books, so 5 pictures are 5 × 2 = 10 books.

items.q: A line plot of ribbon lengths has one X at 1/2 yard and two Xs at 1/4 yard. Laid end to end, how long are those three ribbons together?
misconceptions: dropped one of the quarter pieces
counted an extra quarter
added the tops and the bottoms
correct
items.why: Add the like pieces first: 1/4 + 1/4 = 1/2 yard. Then 1/2 + 1/2 = 1 whole yard.

items.q: A class wants to chart everyone's favorite fruit. Which question gives the best answers to chart?
choices: Why is fruit good for you?
What did you eat on your last birthday?
What is your favorite fruit: apple, banana, grape or pear?
misconceptions: asked for reasons, which a chart cannot count
asked about one day instead of a favorite
asked a yes or no fact instead of a favorite
correct
items.why: A good survey question offers a handful of clear choices that answers can be tallied and charted: apple, banana, grape or pear.

items.q: Six crayons measure 3, 4, 4, 5, 4 and 3 inches. On a line plot of these lengths, how many marks stand over the 4?
misconceptions: counted every crayon, not just the 4-inch ones
counted the 3-inch crayons instead
correct
read the length as the count
items.why: Count the crayons that measure 4 inches: the second, the third and the fifth. That is 3 marks over the 4.

items.q: Your class will make a line plot of everyone's hand spans. What must happen to every hand first?
choices: Measure each one the same way, from the very end
Ask each friend for a number they like
misconceptions: guessed instead of measuring
correct
left most of the data out
collected opinions, not measurements
items.why: A line plot of lengths needs real measurements, all taken the same way, or the marks land in the wrong places.

items.q: A spinner has 8 equal parts and only 1 part is blue. Landing on blue is...
misconceptions: called it certain when only 1 part is blue
called it impossible when blue can land
called it an even chance when only 1 of 8 is blue
correct
items.why: Only 1 of the 8 equal parts is blue, so blue can happen but probably will not: that is unlikely.

items.q: Every face of a cube is painted blue. Rolling a blue face is...
misconceptions: called it likely when blue is the only result
correct
called it unlikely when every face is blue
called it impossible when every face is blue
items.why: Every face is blue, so blue is the only result there can be: that is certain.

items.q: A bag holds 4 red counters and 4 blue counters. Picking a red counter is...
misconceptions: forgot the 4 blue counters
missed that half the counters are red
correct
forgot the 4 red counters
items.why: The bag is split in half: 4 red out of 8 counters. Half and half is an even chance.

items.q: How many grams are in 2 kilograms 600 grams?
misconceptions: shrank the 600 grams to 60
put the 600 in the wrong place
correct
added an extra zero

items.q: A rope 3 meters long is cut into 4 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
misconceptions: glued the numbers together instead of sharing
cut the rope into 3 pieces, not 4
shared out only 1 meter of the 3
correct
items.why: Share 3 meters into 4 equal pieces: each is 3/4 of a meter, and 3/4 of 100 centimeters is 75 centimeters.

items.q: The Vault's last tour starts at 3:50 and lasts 25 minutes. When does it end?
misconceptions: never traded 60 minutes for an hour
stopped 10 minutes early
correct
added 10 minutes too many
items.why: Hop the line: 3:50 plus 10 minutes reaches 4:00, and 15 minutes more lands on 4:15.
